notes.title: The Button Effect - Game Announcement
notes.content:
Hi there!

Today's a big day for me. I've just announced the trailer and title for my new game: [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2299940/The_Button_Effect/]The Button Effect[/url]

After over a year of secretly, quietly working on this new project in Unreal Engine 5, the Steam store-page is now live for wishlisting. If you've enjoyed my previous project, Imagine Lifetimes, this one is something completely different. I've wanted to use my background in Architectural Engineering within my games for a long time now, so I've finally made the switch to 3D by picking up UE5 in the past years.

What makes this project so different?
[list]
[*] [b]Genre:[/b] It's a first-person puzzler (The Witness, The Talos Principle, but on smaller scale).
[*] [b]Engine:[/b] It's a 3D project made in Unreal Engine 5.
[*] [b]Tone:[/b] It's based on a calmer, more gentle and optimistic perspective on life.
[/list]
That doesn't mean there aren't any similarities to be found though! I'm working with voice-actors again, the musician that created the Imagine Lifetimes soundtrack is doing the music, it's going to be a shorter bite-sized experience and there's lots of hidden metaphors throughout this new game.

I know Imagine Lifetimes wasn't perfect or what some players expected from it. I like to think I've learned a lot from all of your feedback to improve my overall game design. It's been a while since you've heard from me here, but I'm hoping you'll be curious to check out my new project?

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/developer/frycandle]You can follow my Steam developer profile to keep an eye on everything I do in the future.[/url]

If minimalist first-person puzzlers happen to be your thing, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2299940/The_Button_Effect/]wishlist The Button Effect on Steam.[/url]

Thanks for all of your support,
- Tim (Frycandle)

notes.title: Imagine Lifetimes - Patch 2.0.2
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36644638/6f4ba5fb013d6b556a4bcf167d6dac5024abdc77.png[/img]

Hey Steam!

This tiny patch is geared towards improving replay-ability for you, allowing you to skip (optional) through the opening credits. These are simple additions, but hopefully they will make your life a bit easier! :)

Most of these hints / skips will only become visible after having at least one ending completed. It made sense to apply this requirement because some things are best not skipped on your very first play. 

[list]
[*] You can now press ENTER during the opening credits to skip ahead
[i](you will see a hint for this during the opening credits after having at least 1 ending completed)[/i]

[*] You can now press ENTER during any of the egg-cell fertilization sequences to skip ahead
[i](you can also click on the fast-forward button during any of the egg-cell fertilization sequences)[/i]

[*] You are no longer required to read the content warning after having at least 1 ending completed
[/list]

Last but not least, you'll notice a teeny tiny visual change inside the light-bulb. Clicking the light-bulb inside the imagination menu (brain) will take you to the hidden backstory. This feature wasn't obvious enough so from now it includes a small arrow animation pointing upwards... *hint-hint!*

[b]Go check it out, only 1% of all total players has uncovered the true ending and finale credits so far! :)[/b]

Cheers,
-Tim (Frycandle)

notes.title: Imagine Lifetimes - Patch 2.0.1
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36644638/36680d4081b018810bce72fdae30cda6fb7dec9f.png[/img]

Hey Steam!

The first 24 hours of the Imagine Lifetimes release are almost behind us. Thank you all so much for the support so far. The game seems stable and no bugs have been reported so far, that's great news!

Based on a handful of reviews, the average playtime and % unlocked of certain achievements, this patch solves some simple but important design flaws. Data shows that when players reach their first ending they assume they've completed the game and quit early. This is a design flaw, because the game has multiple endings (20) and is meant to be played and explored on loop.

With each new ending unlocked, new paths become available throughout and the content intensifies.

[b]The retirement path and ending seemed to be the main culprit. Here's some small but vital fixes:[/b]
[list]
[*] The achievement for this ending unlocked too early prior to dying, this is now fixed
[*] After completing this ending a text will be displayed (Ending 1/20) indicating your progress
[*] If you press quit [X] or clear [C] during this ending sequence, you will skip ahead and be reborn
[*] Once reborn, clicking anything will unlock your imagination, a vital part of the game
[/list]
From now on, as long as you have at least 1 ending completed, you will definitely be able to find the imagination (brain). This is where all your progress is stored, displaying all your completed endings, secrets and challenges. You'll also be able to uncover the main backstory cut-scenes in this menu.

Hopefully these fixes will improve the experience for you. Thank you for your honest feedback and please do keep sending me your thoughts. Your reviews are extremely valuable for the growth of this game. 

[b]If you've played and experienced a good chunk of the game, please consider leaving your review.[/b]

Cheers,
-Tim (Frycandle)

[i]P.S. Special thanks to the ZFAM for waiting on this update! <3[/i]

notes.title: Imagine Lifetimes - Achievements Reveal
notes.content:
Hey Steam!

With the game's launch window now set for Autumn 2020, I wanted to give you a little sneak peek at some of the new stuff I've been adding to the game. This week's reveal is about... achievements! :)

Imagine Lifetimes is a satirical life-simulator in which you make choices and take various paths to find answers. More specifically, you'll find answers to existential questions like 'What is your purpose?'. As you explore and experiment with each lifetime, you will come across one of the (20) multiple endings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36644638/82bb4aed275192d3fefa4d45f72b0b954305863d.png[/img]

After completing your very first ending, you will be able to unlock your 'Imagination' by clicking on the pacifier in the 'Choose your first words.' screen at the start of the game. This will then expose your brain, clicking it will take you deep into the darkest corners of your mind. It is the place where all your progress is stored: every ending, secret and challenge completed. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36644638/4bd9828516c10403cbab0b00bfe680992c901fd5.png[/img]

With 20 unique endings, and 19 additional secrets and challenges, you'll be able to explore and unlock a total of 39 achievements! Each completed ending will be a new piece of the puzzle, unlocking a series of cut-scenes slowly revealing the game's true meaning and backstory.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36644638/5e1de799ce874070b23d3adc18551c1e78187a48.png[/img]

If you manage to find at least 17 endings, you'll be able to enter the game's twentieth ending and finale... 

That story finale is my best kept secret, a twist, inspired by deeply personal experiences. I'm convinced it will completely shake your perspectives on what 'Imagine Lifetimes' is all about. I can't wait to show you!

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1229570/Imagine_Lifetimes/]Thank you for being here, you can Wishlist the game on Steam to stay tuned![/url]
- Tim (Frycandle)

notes.title: Imagine Lifetimes - Launch Delay
notes.content:
Hey Steam, after close consideration I have (unfortunately) decided to postpone the Imagine Lifetimes release date to 'Autumn 2020'. My apologies, I've taken the time to explain in more detail below. <3

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36644638/ec0254a63def7e5b4493859c254e541ae998e3d3.png[/img]

First of all, I'm sorry for the hype these past few weeks. Please know that it was well meant. It just goes to show how much I believed I had this, I really thought I did. I know some of you have been waiting for months or even years to play the full version of the game. I want to thank you for sticking with me all this time, and I hope that you’ll be here for the last stretch of my journey as well.

Over the years of being a solo game developer one tip I’ve read a thousand times over is this: “Do not underestimate the last 10% of development.” Despite having read it over and over, I still failed to grasp its importance...

I get it now, but it seems I had to learn this one the hard way. I underestimated the final stretch, but also the time it takes to single-handedly release a game. I set the September release date at the start of this year as a goal, to motivate and force myself to work towards a launch day. This has been extremely good for me, as I’ve never been more focused on getting things done as much as I have this year. Unfortunately, as the actual date crept closer, I did not want to admit that it was going to be too tight of a squeeze.

I wish I had the knowledge and experience to make this call sooner. Believe me, this whole thing has been one big learning experience for me. It’s my first release, and without a doubt one of the hardest things I’ll ever do. This week has been the tipping point for me though.

Here’s the thing, I work 32 hours a week as a building engineer. This work takes place at my computer at home, due to COVID, at the same desk I do my game-development work. When I finish work on evenings or in the weekends, I never truly ‘leave’ this desk. Instead I spend more of my time sitting on that same chair, working on what I am passionate about. I have recently taken 5 weeks of holiday leave, not to rest, but to work on my game.

Do not get me wrong, I love it. I work hard because I believe in my project, it is the best thing that ever happened to me, creatively speaking. Unfortunately, no matter how passionate I am, there will always be boundaries to how much I can get done within a certain amount of time. Whether it’s for work or my personal stuff, whenever I’m trying to wrap my head around an impossible deadline, it tends to triggers my migraines.

I had a migraine this week, which is the equivalent of my body saying: NOPE.

Imagine Lifetimes development is about 97.5% there. I’m currently working on adding things like the main menu, achievements and the unlockable main story-line cutscenes. I need to add audio to a couple of endings, tie it all together, and the game is ‘done’. It does not sound like a lot, but it adds up. I was trying to squeeze all that into the next two weeks, I shouldn’t.

Not only would I not be able to give it the finishing touch it deserves, I would have jeopardized the quality of my big finale. Everything I’ve worked for these past four years leads up to this moment, it would be such a shame to rush all that just to make it to my self-imposed deadline. I want to keep the quality consistent, I want things to be stable, and most importantly I want to be alive when I finally release my game.

I hope you all agree. <3

In addition to the actual ‘game development’, know that I’ve got plenty of other tasks I do not want to rush or skip out on. This includes everything marketing related, from updating my press-kit, website and game-page to preparing promotional content for social media. There's a lot of 'hidden' work left to do!

The new date is not set in stone to avoid future disappointment, I do not want to make the same mistake twice. I have called it ‘Autumn 2020’, which I consider to be either October or November at the latest. Here's what I'll do:

- I’m going to finish the game.
- I’m going to polish it.
- I’m going to do proper testing to make for a smooth and stable release.
- I’m going to do all of the above in a healthy way.

Once I am 99.9% confident that I am ready for launch, I will announce the date.

Thank you all for being here, I hope you'll understand and please do stay tuned!
- Tim / Frycandle

notes.title: Imagine Lifetimes - Deadly Edition Devlog
notes.content:
What's up Steam,

You might be wondering... why is the final release of Imagine Lifetimes named the 'Deadly Edition'?

( TLDR: [url=https://twitter.com/frycandle/status/1292114212211359751?s=20]see this self-explanatory GIF for #screenshotsaturday[/url] )

[img]https://m.gjcdn.net/content/700/3805376-3kp2rfhj-v4.jpg[/img]

For those of you who have been following the game's developments, you know that Imagine Lifetimes as a life-simulator, has always been inherently deadly.

[b]"The inevitability of death."[/b] is one of the game's main themes.

If you are new to Imagine Lifetimes and this is your first time reading up on it, don't fret! All this deadliness is delivered with a healthy dose of satire: a comical approach along the lines of sarcasm, irony and exaggeration. :-)

For example, you might end up unexpectedly turning into a pile of dust like so:

[img]https://m.gjcdn.net/content/700/3805557-7e92bjkk-v4.png[/img]

Now that particular ending is a literal death, some of you might have already been struck by this one in the 'Early Edition' last year. (let 'em rest in peace)

Even though I've got a handful of brutal and savage literal endings in store for you, guess what I'm even more excited about? Yes, it's metaphorical deaths!

It's these not-so-literal endings that deliver the real philosophical kicker:

[img]https://i.gjcdn.net/data/fireside/posts/27/218/1707718/media/gif_laundry1-bh7bibh2.gif[/img]

Great metaphors leave your head spinning like a load of laundry in a washing machine. It may take some time for their deeper meaning to sink in, but when it finally does... you've got... a pair of clean socks?

...

Speaking of clean socks, you can wishlist Imagine Lifetimes here on Steam:
[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1229570/Imagine_Lifetimes/]https://store.steampowered.com/app/1229570/Imagine_Lifetimes/[/url]

Now, if you'll excuse me, I've got a couple of deadly endings to implement!

Thank you so much for following along, it means a lot. <3
-Frycandle

notes.title: Imagine Lifetimes - Marriage Path Devlog
notes.content:
Hey Steam,

As the release date steadily approaches, I'll be trying to make a habit of doing a couple of extended devlogs for you. I've been quite caught up in some day-job related crunch for some weeks now, but I'm glad to finally see some light at the end of that tunnel. Also, I'll be taking a good chunk of time off in July & August, which will give me plenty of room to breathe while I work to complete the long-awaited Deadly Edition! :)

Alright, I've made a solid amount of progress today so let me show you the upgraded Marriage path. Part of your feedback resulted in me focusing on improving two paths in particular: the Travel and Marriage paths. These paths lacked some consequence (read: deadliness) in the Early Edition, and I'll admit these paths haven't been my main priority in the past.

That changes TO-DAY, check out this brand new mini-game:

[img]https://i.gjcdn.net/data/fireside/posts/25/95/1564595/media/gif_devlog1-w9detwg4.gif[/img]

Side-note: I was thinking recently how I miss the excitement of participating in game-jams, especially since I've been focusing on Imagine Lifetimes for years now. To compensate, I like to think of these in-game mini-games as little game-jams. They allow me to get weirdly creative on a small scale, while also adding value to the long-term project.

Anyways, in order to add some weight to the choices in the Marriage path, I've conjured up this 'memory' based mini-game. Think of it as remembering your partners wishes in terms of wedding plans, in order to keep them happy when the big day comes around. Oh and yes, there is most likely a second ear on the other side spewing out random objects because we all know nobody ever listens...

[img]https://m.gjcdn.net/content/700/3611264-gqkw8n7u-v4.png[/img]

After the Marriage path kicks off with you paying (close) attention to your partner's wishes, the real fun begins! This path is no longer about what YOU want, instead, I'd recommend keeping your significant other as satisfied as possible. You do remember their favorite napkin color, don't you?

[img]https://m.gjcdn.net/content/700/3611265-8gjfjxat-v4.png[/img]

You don't have to get the amount of invitations exactly right, but if you're inviting a handful of guests when your partner expected to entertain half the country... you should start running! Every time you make a somewhat disappointing decision, the pressure gauge will accurately indicate the amount of trouble you're in.

Side note: I'm still debating whether I should add some numbers to that memory based mini-game to indicate the amount of invitations rolling by. There are stacks of 5, 10 and 20 flying across the screen, and the idea is that adding them together results in the (estimated) amount of invitations to be chosen later on. Having a +5 / +10 / +20 pop-up in there might make things more clear to the player, what do you think?

[img]https://m.gjcdn.net/content/700/3611271-tu7un3dy-v4.png[/img]

In addition to the stuff you've seen in the Early Edition, I wanted to add a couple more items to the mix to maintain a healthy amount of replay-ability. These flowers come in various shapes and colors. As you progress throughout the main game (multiple play-through's / marriages), the mini-game difficulty will start ramping up. You'll start getting more variations of items to choose from as things get tougher along the way. I've actually cooked up 4 different difficulties to ease you into the mini-game and throw you off balance as you get comfortable. (you're welcome) :D

[img]https://m.gjcdn.net/content/700/3611267-byewcvgw-v4.png[/img]

That difficulty ramps up in multiple ways, one of which is the increased amount of variations in the items to choose from. Also, on your first time around you will encounter a selection of choices, instead of having to remember every single thing from the get-go.

For example, the 'easy' difficulty in the beginning might be:
Start > Napkins > Cake > Invitations > Finish

The 'normal' difficulty after that could spawn as:
Start > Flowers > Invitations > Cake > Napkins > Finish

When finally the 'hard' and 'insane' difficulties might be:
Start > Flowers > Invitations > Cake > Napkins > USB > Finish

All of which is sprinkled with the usual touch of RNG to keep things fresh and unpredictable. Now, let's take a good look at that pressure gauge:

[img]https://i.gjcdn.net/data/fireside/posts/25/95/1564595/media/gif_devlog3-k9zvbsvq.gif[/img]

The gauge will respond to your decision-making abilities the moment you lock in your choice. If you picked exactly what your partner wanted you to pick, the pressure will drop. If you slip up a little, pressure will start rising a bit. I don't think I have to go into the details of what happens when you royally mess up by picking the absolute worst case scenario four times in a row...

Also, I don't want to tell you just yet because it's meant to be a surprise! ;-)

[img]https://m.gjcdn.net/content/700/3611275-ih9wiqey-v4.jpg[/img]

As you can see I've got most of my to-do list for this particular path ticked off. I'll have to look into adding the win / lose states, where the win state is you getting married happily ever after, and the lose state is... a surprise...

[img]https://m.gjcdn.net/content/700/3611281-qxzstw7d-v4.jpg[/img]

Thought it'd be fun to end on these development notes. I have a huge pile of these scribbles and to-do lists saved up on my desk, and they never really see the light of day. Let me know if you'd like to see some more of that in future devlogs!

Well, well, well... that brings us to the very end of this week's devlog! If you read through this all the way, I appreciate your persistence. Thank you for supporting me on this ridiculous journey called solo game development, I wouldn't be where I am today without you!

P.S. I'll be revealing the Deadly Edition's newly added voice-actor next week (teaser audio included), so get excited! :D

Cheers to you,
-Frycandle

notes.title: Imagine Lifetimes - Game Pitch
notes.content:
Hello Steam Game Festival!

My name is Tim, AKA Frycandle out here on the internet, and I'm the solo game developer currently working on Imagine Lifetimes. After over four years of development, I'm excited to be a part of the Steam Game Festival as we make our way towards the full release in September of this year! 

As physical showcases and conventions have been replaced by digital events like these, I'd love to make the most of this opportunity for us to get to know each other. I'll be readily available to answer any of your questions, you can tune in to the AMA event or shoot me a message at all times. I'd love to hear your honest opinions, thoughts, ideas and experiences on playing the game for the first time. 

Any showcase wouldn't be a proper showcase without what they call the 'elevator pitch'. This is where developers try to pitch their game within a limited amount of time. So, let's pretend you're asking me to pitch the game to you at my imaginary convention booth... What would I tell you?

I think I'd say...

[b]"Imagine Lifetimes is a satirical simulation game about the meaning of life. It's a point-&-click life sim where the choices you make define your path towards one of multiple, equally devastating endings." [/b]


If all that sounds appealing to you, come give it a go! :)

During the festival you'll be able to play the Imagine Lifetimes demo, dubbed the 'Early Edition' out here on Steam for a limited time. This 'Early Edition' build has been out on platforms like GameJolt for a while now, but I can't wait to finally share it out here and connect with the Steam community as well!

Note that the 'Early Edition' is more than a short demo, it's an accurate representation of what the final game will play like. The main game structure is complete, and it's about 50% content complete. The final release of the game will be dubbed the 'Deadly Edition', it'll contain 19 unique endings, main story line progression, path expansions, mini-game improvements and some brand new choices for you to make.

So, without further ado, have a wonderful Steam Game Festival!

-Frycandle
